user: What is the difference between Calico policy Description and Kubernetes policy Description?
assistant: The Calico policy Description refers to the policies that are specific to the Calico network plugin in a Kubernetes cluster. These policies are used to manage and control network traffic in the cluster, allowing or blocking traffic based on network interfaces, pod sources or destinations, and Kubernetes services.
On the other hand, Kubernetes policy Description refers to the policies that are built into Kubernetes and limit access to the Kubernetes Dashboard. These policies are applied at the pod level and affect all classic and VPC clusters. They are used to block all pods from accessing the Kubernetes Dashboard or the dashboard metrics scraper, unless the pod is deployed in a namespace that has the appropriate labels.
In summary, Calico policies are focused on managing and controlling network traffic, while Kubernetes policies are focused on limiting access to the Kubernetes Dashboard.
[The End of Previous Conversation]

[The Start of Current Turn Question]
How does Calico enforce policies?
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
Calico enforces policies through a network plug-in that is integrated with every IBM Cloud Kubernetes Service cluster. It achieves this by implementing Iptables rules, which function as a firewall for the worker node. These rules define the criteria that network traffic must meet in order to be forwarded to the intended resource, including any Kubernetes network policies.
[The End of Reference Answer]
